newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli pharmaceutical sales rose 4.3 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Israeli pharmaceutical sales rose 4.3 pct in 1996.

text.p: Israeli pharmaceutical industry revenues rose 4.3 percent last year to $770 million and will rise eight percent in 1997, Manufacturers Association officials said on Wednesday.
Moshe Manor, head of the association's pharmaceutical division, forecast pharmaceutical exports would grow 10 percent this year but domestic sales would rise just five percent.
He blamed slow local growth on "the government deficit in the field of health and price pressure on manufacturers".

Manor said at a news conference Israeli medicine prices were low by international standards. Nevertheless, he said, a Manufacturers Association study showed Israelis were among the lowest consumers of medicine in the developed world.
The study found Israelis spend $94 a year on medicines compared with $284 by Americans, $245 by the French and $231 by Germans, Manor said.
